verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere documents a dedicated VLM API (`RunAnywhere.vlm`) that takes an image together with a text prompt. The Kotlin SDK docs also state that vision models run on-device with images kept on the phone. missing for 10: documentation of which VLMs are supported and of output or streaming behaviour, cross-platform VLM detail beyond Swift and Kotlin, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run vision-language models that understand images alongside text

citations.quote: `RunAnywhere.vlm` takes an image and a prompt.
The RunAnywhere Kotlin SDK runs language, speech, and vision models on the device. Prompts, audio, and images stay on the phone
